# Superstore PBIP test sample

A Power BI project (PBIP) built to match `Superstore_Tableau2024_3.twbx`. It reads the same data
already loaded in Snowflake, `WBR_DB.PUBLIC.SAMPLE_SUPERSTORE` (10,194 rows). It is the first test
input for the Power BI parser.

**Status: generated by script and not yet opened in Power BI Desktop.** All 41 JSON files pass
Microsoft's published PBIR/PBIP JSON schemas. Those schemas don't cover the TMDL model files or the
per-visual role names (`Category`, `Y`, `Values`, ...), so both stay unverified until Desktop opens
the project.

- Report: PBIR format (`Superstore.Report/definition/...`), 5 pages, 28 visuals.
- Model: TMDL format (`Superstore.SemanticModel/definition/...`). It has 2 tables, 12 measures,
  2 calculated columns, a calculated date table, 1 relationship and 1 RLS role.
- Regenerate: `python gen_pbip.py <out_dir>`. Check: `python validate_pbip.py <schemas_dir> <pbip_dir>`.
  Both scripts are in `../tools/`.

## Open it in Power BI Desktop

1. Use a Power BI Desktop release from September 2026 or later, since PBIR is the default format
   from then on. Older releases need File > Options > Preview features >
   "Power BI Project (.pbip) save option" and "Store reports using enhanced metadata format (PBIR)"
   switched on.
2. Open `Superstore.pbip`.
3. Go to Transform data > Edit parameters and set `SnowflakeServer` to your account host
   (`<account>.snowflakecomputing.com`). Check `SnowflakeWarehouse` (POWERHOUSE),
   `SnowflakeDatabase` (WBR_DB) and `SnowflakeSchema` (PUBLIC).
4. Refresh. Sign in to Snowflake when prompted.
5. Check the numbers below. If anything fails, send the error text or a screenshot. Then use
   File > Save once: Desktop rewrites the files in its own canonical form, and comparing that output
   against these files is the best schema evidence we can get.

## Expected numbers (all data, no filters)

These come from the source data and match `DEMO.md`.

| Measure | Expected |
| --- | --- |
| Total Sales | 2,326,534.35 |
| Total Profit | 292,296.81 |
| Profit Ratio | 12.6% |
| Total Quantity | 38,654 |
| Order Count | 5,111 |
| Customer Count | 804 |
| Furniture Sales | 754,747.76 |
| Avg Days to Ship | 3.96 |
| Sales, Central / East / South / West | 503,170.67 / 691,828.17 / 391,721.90 / 739,813.61 |

Snowflake check:

```sql
SELECT SUM(SALES), SUM(PROFIT), SUM(PROFIT)/SUM(SALES), SUM(QUANTITY),
       COUNT(DISTINCT ORDER_ID), COUNT(DISTINCT CUSTOMER_ID)
FROM WBR_DB.PUBLIC.SAMPLE_SUPERSTORE;
```

## Mapping from the Tableau workbook

| Tableau dashboard | Power BI page | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Overview | Overview | Map replaced by a bar chart of sales by state. Map visuals need tenant map settings. |
| Customers | Customers | Scatter, ranked bar, region columns |
| Shipping | Shipping | Gantt not converted. The trend is a line of average days to ship. |
| Order Details | Order Details | Table plus four slicers |
| Performance (sales vs target, a Tableau blend) | Performance | Replaced by sales vs last year: `SALES_TARGET` has no single-column key to relate to |
| Commission Model, Forecast, What If Forecast, Product | not converted | What-if parameters, forecasting and heatmap are out of MVP scope |

## Answer key for the parser

This is the support level each item should get from the Power BI converter, per the plan's matrix.

| Item | Expected class |
| --- | --- |
| Total Sales, Total Profit, Profit Ratio, Total Quantity, Order Count, Customer Count, Avg Discount, Sales per Customer | Auto |
| Furniture Sales (CALCULATE with a constant filter) | Partial |
| Avg Days to Ship (AVERAGEX iterator) | Manual |
| Sales LY, Sales YoY % (time intelligence, VAR) | Manual |
| Days to Ship, Order Profitable (calculated columns) | Partial |
| Date (calculated table) | Unsupported, but the relationship to it must be reported |
| Role "Central Region" (`Orders[Region] = "Central"`) | Partial: generated row access policy for review |
| Combo chart, matrix (Performance page) | Partial |
| Area, bar, column, line, scatter, card, table, slicer | Auto |
| 100% stacked bar | Partial |

## Troubleshooting: ODBC "REST request ... failed: HTTP error - code=404"

Snowflake returns 404 when the account in `SnowflakeServer` does not exist, so the request never reaches login or the warehouse.
Set `SnowflakeServer` (Transform data > Edit parameters) to the host only, in the form `<orgname>-<accountname>.snowflakecomputing.com`.
Leave out `https://`, any path, and `/console`. An old-style locator needs its region, for example `xy12345.us-east-2.aws.snowflakecomputing.com`.
The other three parameters are plain names: warehouse `POWERHOUSE`, database `WBR_DB`, schema `PUBLIC`. A wrong warehouse gives a different error after login, not a 404.
